clue.text: Possibly scuba buddy's inside empty aquarium

indicators.note: inside says the buddy sits within the emptied aquarium
an empty aquarium keeps only its shell, the outside letters of the word

parts.note: a crony is a close pal or buddy

explanation.surface: A diver's companion is floating about in a drained fish tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks scuba as an example: the word was formed from the initials of self-contained underwater breathing apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba is a word built from initial letters, so it is one example of this kind of abbreviation.

clue.text: Distinct foreign car ran endlessly

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: endlessly removes the last letter of the verb

parts.note: colours that ran bled

explanation.surface: A distinctive German car kept running without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear, distinct sound is one that can be plainly heard.

clue.text: Beginning to roll joints creates irritation

indicators.note: Beginning to takes just the opening letter of roll

parts.note: ankles are joints of the leg

explanation.surface: Someone starting to roll a cannabis joint annoys the people around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll joints' suggests making cigarettes; the joints are body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles keeps annoying a person, causing lasting resentment.

clue.text: Disadvantaged born with case of deficiency

parts.note: née, used before a maiden name, means born

indicators.note: case of takes the outer letters of deficiency, its casing

explanation.surface: A child born with a vitamin deficiency starts life at a disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor people lacking essentials are deprived or disadvantaged.

clue.text: City, German city, mostly one leading knees-up

indicators.note: leading puts the numeral ahead of the next piece
mostly drops the final letter of the city's name

parts.note: Munich is a city in Bavaria
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: up in a down entry means reading from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a lap is the top of the thighs and knees when sitting

explanation.surface: A German city mostly leads the knees-up of Oktoberfest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knees-up', British slang for a party, is split: knees gives LAP and up turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal is the adjective for a town or city, as in a city council.

clue.text: Remember a test employing slates?

indicators.note: the words Remember a test employ, or contain, the letters needed, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A schoolchild is told to recall a test that used old-fashioned writing slates.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is British informal for criticising harshly, the same as scolding.

clue.text: Isolated hill side finally south of base

indicators.note: south of in a down entry places the letter below the first piece

parts.note: the butt is the thick base end of a rifle or tool

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of side

explanation.surface: A lone hill rises on the far side, south of the army base.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped hill standing alone on a plain, common in the American West.

clue.text: Forward adult wearing ruddy frock!

indicators.note: wearing means the adult letter is put on inside the colour word

parts.note: ruddy means red
A is the film classification for adult
a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: A grown-up is wearing a bright red frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' is the verb, as in forwarding a letter to a new address.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward post is to send it on to a new place, putting a fresh address on it.

clue.text: Boss in argument about digital protection providers

indicators.note: about turns the whole combined piece round
in places the boss inside the quarrel

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
a CEO is a chief executive, the boss

explanation.surface: A boss caught in a row over online security software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computing, but digits are toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel caps in work boots shield the toes, which are digits of the foot.

clue.text: Waiter is tough blowing top after dish

indicators.note: after puts the shortened tough word after the dish

parts.note: a stew is a dish of slow-cooked food

indicators.note: blowing top loses the first letter, the top of a down word

parts.note: hard means tough

explanation.surface: A waiter loses his temper over a tough piece of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' looks like losing one's temper; it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship or plane an attendant serving food and drink is a waiter.

clue.text: Waste time in prison

parts.note: dung is animal waste
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone complains that time spent in jail is wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste time' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell in a castle, a kind of jail.

clue.text: Role is turning with facility expressed on this?

definitions.text: Role is turning with facility expressed on this?

indicators.note: turning says the word for a role is read backwards

parts.note: a part is an actor's role

indicators.note: expressed means the synonym for facility is spoken, giving letters that sound like it

parts.note: facility, as in doing something with facility, means ease

explanation.surface: An acrobat spins through the air with apparent ease on the swinging bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a circus performer turning with ease is doing so on a swinging bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The circus bar hung from ropes is where an aerialist turns somersaults with practised ease.

clue.text: Ship nearly caught by Siren's lament

indicators.note: caught by says the shortened ship sits held inside the siren

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful, alluring woman, a siren

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the vessel's name is dropped

parts.note: a yacht is a sailing ship

explanation.surface: A sailor is lured almost onto the rocks by a singing Siren of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to grumble or moan is the same as to complain or lament.

clue.text: Upset American disturbed admitting Republican crisis

indicators.note: admitting means the reversed piece lets the Republican letter in
upset in a down-or-across sense means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: mad means mentally disturbed

explanation.surface: An agitated American is upset at a crisis involving a Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting or tense situation, a crisis in everyday speech.

clue.text: A leader of socialists in spot over moderates

indicators.note: in places the A and the socialists' first letter within the reversed verb
over means the word for spot is turned back to front

parts.note: to spot is to see

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of socialists

explanation.surface: A left-wing leader in a tight spot ends up overruling party moderates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moderates' looks like a noun for centrists; it is a verb meaning lessens.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate pain or tension is to lessen or relieve it, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Stern well-balanced circling round island

indicators.note: circling means the sound-minded word goes round the next two pieces

parts.note: a sane person is mentally well-balanced
a turn is a round or rotation

explanation.surface: A steady sailor circles round an island at the back of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like the back of a ship; it is the adjective for grim.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloomy, grave person has a forbidding, stern manner.

clue.text: Goddesses so powerful holding back infatuated

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in reverse order
holding means the words Goddesses so powerful contain the letters in a run

explanation.surface: Mighty goddesses of myth are holding back an infatuated suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone possessed by a passion is utterly gripped or obsessed, as an infatuated lover is.

clue.text: Son unlucky to embrace sweetheart that's dumpy

indicators.note: to embrace means the unlucky word wraps around the heart letter

parts.note: hapless means unlucky
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: An unlucky son has to embrace his dumpy girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumpy figure is short and thick, lacking any trim form.

clue.text: Hint offence involves Conservative — upset everyone with it

indicators.note: involves means the offence wraps round the Conservative letter

parts.note: a sin is an offence against morality

indicators.note: upset turns the following words for everyone and it back to front

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A Tory gives offence with a hint, and everyone is upset about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace or the faintest bit of something, as in not a hint of truth.

clue.text: Raced around block sharing parking and crashed

indicators.note: around means the speeding word goes round the block

parts.note: sped means raced

indicators.note: sharing parking means the block's P is shared with the P of the other word, so written once

parts.note: a lump is a solid block

explanation.surface: A car raced around the block, shared a parking spot and crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To slump is to collapse heavily, as an exhausted person crashes onto a sofa.

clue.text: Sort of painting in my opinion's about done

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation goes around the done word

parts.note: IMO is the texting abbreviation for in my opinion
past means done, over

explanation.surface: An art critic pronounces a style of painting done for.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique of laying paint on thickly so brushstrokes stand out from the canvas.

clue.text: Seal starts to swim in glacial icy lake

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letter of each of the five following words

explanation.surface: A seal begins a swim in an icy glacial lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The seal looks like the animal, but it is the stamp used to mark wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigil is an inscribed symbol or signet mark, the kind of device pressed into wax.

clue.text: Deity without love with Echo for so long

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the deity surrounds the love

parts.note: a god is a deity
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
by can mean with, as in by hand
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A god without love, together with the nymph Echo, pines for so long.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is a casual way of saying farewell.

clue.text: They may rent B&B, for instance

definitions.meaning: people who let out property, who rent it to others
B and B are characters of the alphabet, examples of written symbols

explanation.surface: Guesthouse owners letting rooms as a bed and breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords who let rooms are those who let, and B is a symbol of the alphabet.

clue.text: High tea missing starter

indicators.note: missing starter drops the first letter of the meal's name

parts.note: in parts of Britain tea is the evening meal, supper

explanation.surface: High tea is served without the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High tea' reads as the British afternoon meal, but High is the definition. In northern Britain 'tea' is the main evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper and high both describe something at a greater height, as in the top deck.

clue.text: Ship's second crew facing stick hiding nothing

indicators.note: facing places the crew ahead of the stick in the answer

parts.note: a team is a crew of workers

indicators.note: hiding means the stick conceals the zero inside it

parts.note: a bat is a stick used in cricket or baseball
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A ship's second crew confronts someone hiding nothing but a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer or other vessel driven by steam is a type of ship.

clue.text: Following Church upholding transgression

indicators.note: upholding in a down entry means the church sits beneath and holds up the sin

parts.note: a sin is a transgression
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Following church teaching, someone defends a wrongdoer's transgression.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition, since means after or following, as in since the war.

clue.text: Crazy old lady needs innumerable cats initially

parts.note: one's old lady is informal for one's mother, ma

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the last three words

explanation.surface: A dotty old woman needs countless cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild, frenzied behaviour is crazy or frantic.

clue.text: No one's fool going back for love

indicators.note: going back means the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: one is I, and the apostrophe s gives S
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: Nobody is fool enough to go back to an old love.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense romantic feeling or ardour is a strong form of love.

clue.text: Honour men led without cover taking big shot

indicators.note: taking means the uncovered letters take in the big shot
without cover strips the outside letters from the phrase men led

parts.note: a nob is a person of wealth or rank, a big shot

explanation.surface: Soldiers led without cover are honoured for taking on a big gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage or dignify them is to honour them.

clue.text: See duck in chop suey occasionally

indicators.note: in says the duck is placed within the chopping word

parts.note: to dice food is to chop it into cubes
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

indicators.note: occasionally takes only some letters of suey, the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A Chinese takeaway menu offers duck in chop suey.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's area of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district under that bishop's charge, the same thing as a diocese.

clue.text: Work out including cycles oddly for victory

indicators.note: including means the verb for work out holds the picked letters

parts.note: to suss something is informal British for working it out

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of cycles

explanation.surface: A cyclist's oddly erratic workout still leads to a win.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph or win, as when a venture comes off well.
